findings.title: Omfattende uautoriseret adgang til borgeres CPR-oplysninger
findings.summary_md: The CPR administration's own advisory, published 5 October 2026, states that misuse of a Danish company's lawful search access to the CPR system gave unauthorized parties names, addresses, and CPR numbers for about 8.8 million registered citizens. It confirms the company's access was stopped, the incident was reported to the Datatilsynet, and police are investigating with other authorities. People registered with name and address protection were not covered by the unauthorized access.

findings.title: Denmark CPR data breach: attackers abused a firm's access, leaving CPR numbers exposed for 8.8 million people. Here is what to know and do.
findings.summary_md: Early coverage explaining that attackers abused a firm's legitimate access to the national register rather than exploiting a flaw in the register itself, leaving CPR numbers exposed for 8.8 million people. The piece includes practical guidance for residents on what the breach means and what to do.

findings.title: Denmark Confirms Major Security Incident Exposing 8.8 Million Citizen Records
findings.summary_md: Reports Denmark's confirmation of unauthorized access to the Central Person Register affecting about 8.8 million registered individuals, including names, residential addresses, and CPR numbers. Notes the impact figure exceeds Denmark's current population.

findings.title: CPR data breach exposes personal details of 8.8 million people in Denmark
findings.summary_md: First Danish English-language coverage of the disclosure, reporting that the CPR data breach exposed personal details of 8.8 million people in Denmark. Published the same day authorities confirmed the incident.

findings.title: Denmark population registry data breach affects 8.8 million people
findings.summary_md: Reports the CPR warning that roughly 8.8 million people, about 80 percent of the 11 million records in the register, had personal information exposed. Describes the attack as abuse of a private company's legitimate access rather than a compromise of the registry itself.

findings.title: Recent Danish PII Exposures Increase Risk of Targeted Phishing Campaigns
findings.summary_md: Assessment arguing the exposed CPR data raises the risk of targeted phishing, social engineering, impersonation, and identity fraud, and can validate or enrich information obtained from other sources. Notes authorities revoked the company's access, reported the incident to the Danish Data Protection Agency, and opened an investigation with law enforcement.
